title: Invariant ring and canonical invariant-spectrum map of an affine scheme action
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $E$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $H$ a group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme] with a left action $a:H\times_k U\to U$ on $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Scheme products and their projections are [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\iota_E:E\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ be the canonical coordinate identification. Set $\rho=(a\circ\mathrm{swap})^*\circ\iota_E$ and $j=\operatorname{pr}_U^*\circ\iota_E$, maps from $E$ to $\Gamma(U\times_kH,\mathcal O)$. Define the actual subring $E^H=\{e\in E:\rho(e)=j(e)\}$ as the ring equalizer. Constants lie in this subring because both morphisms are over $k$; restrict the specified map $k\to E$ to $k\to E^H$. Define the $k$-scheme $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(E^H)$ with that structural map and $q:U\to Y$ to be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the inclusion $E^H\hookrightarrow E$, as a morphism over $k$. No smoothness, affineness or finite-type hypothesis on $H$, finite-type hypothesis on $E$, or finite generation of $E^H$ is part of these constructions.
